To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diffraction of Gaussian laser beams by uniform volume Bragg grating (VBG) in photo-thermo-refractive (PTR) glasses can be modeled by Kogelnik’s theory of coupled waves, and that the model results agree with the experimental data for high-efficiency Bragg gratings.

the angular and spectral selectivities of volume Bragg gratins are determined by the ratio of beam quality and grating quality, and the beam quality is determined by the ratio between the beam divergence and spectral width.
the angular and spectral selectivities of volume gratings in PTR-glass are sufficient to achieve diffraction of Gaussian beam in the Bragg resonance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of Gaussian beam diffration on volume Bragg grating in PTR glass.
the study of volume Bragg gratins in PTR glass and their application for laser beam processing.
the development of new types of Bragg gratings with high efficiency of diffraction of laser radiation in PTR glass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bragg gratings can be considered as a high efficient and versatile element for beam shaping, beam combining and beam steering.
the model developed in this work can be applied to describe diffraction of Gaussian beam on volume Bragg grating in any material with a high degree of precision.
the PTR glass is an excellent material for the fabrication of volume Bragg gratins for the application in high power lasers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the diffraction of Gaussian laser beams on Bragg gratings.
the diffraction efficiency of the Bragg grating in PTR glass is high enough (up to 90%) for the case of the Gaussian beam with the divergence of 0.1° and the spectral width of 0.5nm.
the diffraction of Gaussian beam on uniform volume Bragg grating in PTR glass is a very effective way to produce a narrow beam with high intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular and spectral selectivities are the main parameters of a grating, which should be considered when designing a grating for a given application.

Bragg grating diffraction of Gaussian beam is possible only if angular selectivity of the grating is smaller than angular beam divergence, while spectral selectivity of the Bragg grating should be larger than spectral beam width.
for a given spectral width of the Gaussian beam, the angular divergence of the beam must be less than the angular width of the Bragg grating in order to obtain Bragg diffraction of the beam.
